NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders,
  City Council Members will be participating via teleconference.

  - City Council meetings are recorded and live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and
  available for viewing thereafter, and televised on Cox 33 and Frontier FiOS 38 on Wednesday and Friday
  following the meeting.

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone,
  Meeting ID: 854 2446 3341, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to
  speak using the call-in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. the night of the Council meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 854 2446 3341, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MAY 11, 2021

 1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

 A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
 by MAYOR ZUCKERMAN at 7:04 p.m. via teleconference, pursuant to the Governor’s
 Executive Order N-29-20 and current State and County Public Health Orders.

 2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Flag Salute led by Boy Scouts of America, Cub Scout Pack 970

 3.  ROLL CALL

 City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan & Zuckerman

 City Council Members Absent:  None

 City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Interim City Clerk Carrie Gallagher

 4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS
 A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2021 "MENTAL HEALTH AWARENESS
  MONTH"

 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN declared May as Mental Health Awareness Month.

 B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 2021 "MATERNAL MENTAL HEALTH
  AWARENESS MONTH"

 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN introduced COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ who shared her
 personal experience. She acknowledged the importance of Maternal Mental Health and
 provided resources.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ introduced Dr. Ellie Berkowitz-Handler and Ashley
McCarthy, both members of the non-profit “Maternal Mental Health Awareness Now” who
shared their personal experiences and remarked on the stigma and reluctance to discuss
this topic and shared hopes for more open communication amongst those who most need it.

 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA noted her appreciation for both the Maternal Mental Health
 and Mental Health Proclamations. She added that the more that we discuss mental health,
 the better prepared we will be down the line in helping those who have suffered
 substantially throughout the COVID-19 pandemic.

 C.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING MAY 15, 2021 "KIDS TO PARKS DAY"

 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN declared May 15 as Kids to Parks Day.

 5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

 The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority
 consent of the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good
 cause is shown by a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual
 consideration will be voted on separately.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA,
  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-H AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MAY 11, 2021
   AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS - APRIL 2021 AND MAY 2021

  APPROVE WARRANTS 63876 THROUGH 63933 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $482,434.82 AND SUPPLEMENTAL WARRANTS 040621 THROUGH 040721;
  050121 IN THE AMOUNT OF $81,022.11 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $563,456.93 WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  SPECIAL JOINT CITY COUNCIL & PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF APRIL 26, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF MAY 5, 2021

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

NONE.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ANNUAL AUDIT SERVICES AGREEMENT

Recommendation: That the City of Rolling Hills Estates approve the agreement per City
Attorney’s approval and rates for the CPA firm of Rogers, Anderson, Malody & Scott, LLP to
perform annual audit and report for the Fiscal Year 2020-21 not to exceed $42,300, prepare
the Pepper Tree Foundation’s tax returns in an amount not to exceed $1,845, and review the
GANN appropriation limitation.

Administrative Services Director, Michael Whitehead, provided a staff report (as per the
agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that Exhibit A was not included as an attachment in the
agreement. Administrative Services Director, Michael Whitehead indicated that it was not
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MAY 11, 2021
  included because of the various staff members that are utilized on the firms end. He
 indicated that a team comes out to conduct the audit and their hours vary based on what
 they need to work on at the time of audit.

 City Attorney, Don Davis, clarified that Exhibit A is the scope of services, fees and
 personnel, which is the agreement itself, though it is not in the place indicated on the
 agreement table of contents.

 COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF noted that the positions and associated fees should be
 indicated in the document. City Manager Grammer added that staff would amend the
 agreement to include key personnel & hourly rates.

 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked Administrative Services Director if there were any new rules
 of procedures related to the Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB).
 Administrative Services Director Whitehead responded that there is a pronouncement that
 requires governmental agencies have to declare all leases from a “copier to land.” He noted
 that is new for this year’s audit and documents have already been delivered to auditors.

 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN asked if these would now be recorded as liabilities. Administrative
 Services Director, Mike Whitehead affirmed.

 MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted that for large cities the information would be useful for people
 to have and the process would likely become natural.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED THE AGREEMENT PER CITY ATTORNEY’S APPROVAL AND
  RATES FOR THE CPA FIRM OF ROGERS, ANDERSON, MALODY &
  SCOTT, LLP TO PERFORM ANNUAL AUDIT AND REPORT FOR THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2020-21, PREPARE THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION’S
  TAX RETURNS, AND REVIEW THE GANN APPROPRIATION LIMITATION as
  amended; TO INCLUDE UPDATED EXHIBIT A WITH KEY PERSONNEL &
  HOURLY RATES.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

Public comment was invited via email, via eComment on the City’s website, and during the live
Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social media platforms.

No public testimony was received.

 9.  OLD BUSINESS
 A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER AND STATUS OF
  CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

 City Manager Grammer reported that last week Los Angeles County moved into the least
 restrictive yellow tier in the State’s blueprint for a safer economy. This allows for increased
 indoor capacity at restaurants, fitness centers, movie theaters, museums, and more. The
 FDA announced this week that they have now expanded emergency authorization use of
 the Pfizer vaccine for adolescents, aged 12 to 15, which could begin before the end of the
 week. He noted that vaccines are now widely available at most locations without having to
 make an appointment. He added that vaccination rates countywide are at about 58% of
 individuals 16 and older who have received at least one dose, however, RHE is at 74%
 adding that the City is outpacing the rest of the County.

City Manager Grammer reported that the City is moving forward with the Mayor's Breakfast
Ride scheduled for July 10 to be held as usual with the exception of the pancake breakfast.
He noted that a modified grab-n-go version of the breakfast would replace what has been
done in the past. Additionally, he reported that The Hills are Alive race is scheduled for
August 7 at Ernie Howlett Park, and the Tracy Austin Doubles Tennis Tournament has been
pushed to the fall, with a date yet to be determined.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MAY 11, 2021
 10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS
COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported having attended the Neighborhood Council meeting
adding that the July 4th holiday was discussed. She stated that very few of the
neighborhoods at this point are planning any group gatherings. She voiced the group’s
concern over fireworks and the potential for fire during this dry season. She requested that
the City to do some website advisements on the issue and suggested that Sheriff’s
Department volunteers could be of help tracking down the source of nightly fireworks in the
area. Additionally, she reported an increase of coyote sightings and missing pets.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported attending the South Bay Cities Council of Governments
(SBCCOG) Steering Committee and noted discussion regarding increased coyote sightings.
Educational programs, hazing and alternatives to trapping were all discussed. She shared
that the Steering Committee recommended re-appointment of Mayor Pro Tem Frank
Zerunyan as the COG’s representative to SCAG.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reported having attended the Palos Verdes Legislative
Committee meeting noting they voted to support Assemblyman Muratsuchi’s AB 1251
regarding localized public health orders. Additionally, she noted the re-opening of local
schools, the scheduling of graduation ceremonies and proms and added that with the
reported 5% loss of students, the district will be asking the state to allow students the option
to continue home studies if they wished to do so.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted having attended the SCAG General Assembly and
added that there is new leadership with the appointment of a new president. Additionally,
there were several bylaw changes made mostly with respect to topics that relate to equity,
inclusion, and bylaw procedural issues.

MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN reported on the California Contract Cities Association
upcoming installation of the incoming president, Lomita Mayor Mark Waronek, noting the
installation will be virtual and invited everyone to attend. He added that he feels encouraged
reading about the County likely reaching herd immunity soon and is hopeful life will return
to normal by this coming summer.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted having attended the Traffic and Safety Committee meeting.
He discussed the proposal of adding signs to notify exiting and approaching cars of the
bicycle and equestrian pathways, however the Committee felt that signs would not be
necessary; instead, the Committee recommended that the crosswalk be more clearly
marked, and the surrounding vegetation trimmed. He noted the results of the speed study
and that no changes were recommended in our speed limits.

MAYOR ZUCKERMAN thanked City Attorney Davis and City Manager Grammer for having
met with him to discuss issues related to Vector Control. He added that the Clean Power
Alliance had a rate setting meeting noting that residents will see a rate increase primarily
due to Southern California Edison rate increase, due to hardening the grid which will cause
distribution and transmission cost increases. He added that there were several proposals
on how to deal with the rates for power. The outcome was favorable to green cities such as
ours so that we will remain in the as-advertised bracket, with respect to pricing relative to
Edison.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

NONE.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MAY 11, 2021
  14.  ADJOURNMENT
At 7:43 p.m. with no objection, MAYOR ZUCKERMAN adjourned the City Council meeting to the next
meeting: Tuesday, May 25, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. via teleconference.

 Submitted by,  Approved by,

 Carrie Gallagher  Steve Zuckerman
 Interim City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MAY 11, 2021
